title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Fathers close: Actual reconciliation needs the receiver’s consent
pass_a_gloss: From orthodox antiquity therefore they have departed who state that by the very passion of Christ all humans are placed in the state of grace; nor less those who teach that the predestinate themselves in this death of Christ obtained remission of their sins, or justification and reconciliation with God, from eternity: since this justification or actual reconciliation (as Bernard truly and skillfully) cannot be of the receiver without consent any more than without the grace of the giver. And thus you have received our sentence confirmed, and the contrary enervated (enervatam).
pass_b_english: From orthodox antiquity, therefore, they have departed who state that by the very passion of Christ all human beings are placed in the state of grace; nor less those who teach that the predestinate themselves, in this death of Christ, obtained the remission of their sins, or justification and reconciliation with God, from eternity — since this justification or actual reconciliation (as Bernard truly and skillfully) cannot belong to the receiver without consent any more than without the grace of the giver.
And thus you have received our sentence confirmed, and the contrary enervated.
source_text: Ab orthodoxa ergo antiquitate desciverunt, qui statuunt ipsa passione Christi omnes homines in statum gratiae repositos; nec minus illi, qui docent ipsos praedestinatos in hac morte Christi consecutos remissionem peccatorum suorum, sive justificationem & reconciliationem cum Deo, ab aeterno: cum haec justificatio sive actualis reconciliatio (ut vere & scite Bernardus) tam absque consensu non potest esse recipientis, quam absque gratia dantis. Atque sic accepistis sententiam nostram confirmatam, atque enervatam contrariam.
